headline_marked: PM Tarique outlines [[3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh]] at UNGA
headline: PM Tarique outlines 3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh at UNGA
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman presents a plan for recovery, restoration, and reconstruction to repair the country after years of fascist rule.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, outlining a '3-R strategy'—recovery, restoration, and reconstruction—to repair Bangladesh.
The Prime Minister stated that after freeing itself from enforced disappearances, killings, and corruption, the country is once again embarking on the path of democracy.
To transform the working-age population into skilled human resources, the government has allocated US$50 million this fiscal year for young entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators.
A strong focus on women's empowerment was highlighted, with priorities on education, employment, and expanded cash financing for women in small and medium-sized industries.
The government is introducing social protection initiatives, including Family, Farmers', Sports, and e-Health Cards, to ensure the benefits of economic growth reach every citizen.
Education spending is planned to increase to 5% of GDP within five years, with a new curriculum emphasizing technical and practical education to improve employment prospects.
On the global stage, the PM called for the resolution of conflicts through dialogue and diplomatic processes to mitigate humanitarian crises and global economic pressure.
The government's 31-point programme is aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals' 'Leave No One Behind' theme to reduce urban-rural disparities.
caption:
Recovery, restoration, and reconstruction. PM Tarique Rahman unveils a 3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh at the UN General Assembly.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, outlining a '3-R strategy'—recovery, restoration, and reconstruction—to repair Bangladesh.

The Prime Minister stated that after freeing itself from enforced disappearances, killings, and corruption, the country is once again embarking on the path of democracy.

To transform the working-age population into skilled human resources, the government has allocated US$50 million this fiscal year for young entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators.

A strong focus on women's empowerment was highlighted, with priorities on education, employment, and expanded cash financing for women in small and medium-sized industries.

The government is introducing social protection initiatives, including Family, Farmers', Sports, and e-Health Cards, to ensure the benefits of economic growth reach every citizen.

Education spending is planned to increase to 5% of GDP within five years, with a new curriculum emphasizing technical and practical education to improve employment prospects.

On the global stage, the PM called for the resolution of conflicts through dialogue and diplomatic processes to mitigate humanitarian crises and global economic pressure.

The government's 31-point programme is aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals' 'Leave No One Behind' theme to reduce urban-rural disparities.

headline_marked: Fuel price hike: [[Vegetables and fish prices rise]] in Dhaka markets
headline: Fuel price hike: Vegetables and fish prices rise in Dhaka markets
summary: Rising transport costs following the government's fuel price increase have pushed up the cost of essential food items, while bottled soybean oil supplies dwindle.
details: Following the government's decision to increase fuel prices last Sunday, the cost of various vegetables and fish has risen in Dhaka's markets. Diesel prices rose from 115 to 135 BDT per liter, while petrol and octane now cost 160 BDT and 165 BDT per liter respectively.

The hike in fuel costs has led to increased truck rentals, raising prices at every stage from production centers to wholesale and retail markets. Several vegetables have seen price increases of 5 to 20 BDT per kg, with eggplants rising to 100-160 BDT per kg.
Fish prices have also climbed by 20 to 50 BDT per kg. Shing fish is now selling around 500 BDT per kg, while prices for Koi, Pabda, Shrimp, Tilapia, Pangas, and Rui fish have also increased.
Other essentials remain high; open flour has increased by 5 BDT and maida by 10 BDT per kg over the last month. Broiler chickens are selling at 180-200 BDT per kg, and eggs at 150 BDT per dozen.

There is a noticeable shortage of 1 and 2-liter bottled soybean oil, with 5-liter bottles also seeing reduced supply. Bottled soybean oil was priced at 204 BDT per liter after a 5 BDT increase earlier this month.
Retailers claim that companies are limiting the supply of oil to the market. Dealers suggest that companies may be intending to further increase the price of soybean oil.
caption:
Fuel prices go up, and now your grocery bill is too. Vegetables and fish prices are climbing across Dhaka.

Following the government's decision to increase fuel prices last Sunday, the cost of various vegetables and fish has risen in Dhaka's markets. Diesel prices rose from 115 to 135 BDT per liter, while petrol and octane now cost 160 BDT and 165 BDT per liter respectively.

The hike in fuel costs has led to increased truck rentals, raising prices at every stage from production centers to wholesale and retail markets. Several vegetables have seen price increases of 5 to 20 BDT per kg, with eggplants rising to 100-160 BDT per kg.

Fish prices have also climbed by 20 to 50 BDT per kg. Shing fish is now selling around 500 BDT per kg, while prices for Koi, Pabda, Shrimp, Tilapia, Pangas, and Rui fish have also increased.

Other essentials remain high; open flour has increased by 5 BDT and maida by 10 BDT per kg over the last month. Broiler chickens are selling at 180-200 BDT per kg, and eggs at 150 BDT per dozen.

There is a noticeable shortage of 1 and 2-liter bottled soybean oil, with 5-liter bottles also seeing reduced supply. Bottled soybean oil was priced at 204 BDT per liter after a 5 BDT increase earlier this month.

Retailers claim that companies are limiting the supply of oil to the market. Dealers suggest that companies may be intending to further increase the price of soybean oil.
